purpose: Enter a password using a native TextInput with an explicit accessible reveal or conceal action.
behaviorProvider: Native TextInput and its public Field integration, composed with the shared IconButton; local visibility state only.

component: native input composition and forwarded ref
effective Field disabled state shared by both controls
host: accepted controlled value and native form lifecycle
accessible names, password policy and autocomplete intent
authentication, storage and any conceal-on-navigation policy

requirements.statement: Start each mounted instance with native input type password. Reveal and conceal change that same TextInput's type between text and password without replacing the value model.
Forward value, defaultValue, onValueChange and native onChange unchanged to TextInput. Visibility changes update only local visibility state and must not synthesize value-change events.
When value is supplied, accept edits through a change callback and feed the resulting value back. defaultValue initializes the uncontrolled value; it is not a later reset command.

Forward the public ref to TextInput's native input and preserve ordinary input properties and lifecycle handlers, including name, form, autocomplete, required and validation constraints. Reserve type and suffix for password visibility and keep clear controls disabled.

Use the same effective Field control id and disabled precedence for the input and visibility action. Let TextInput retain standalone or Field labeling, merged descriptions, required and invalid metadata; explicit control props retain useFieldControl precedence.

Render a real IconButton with type button, an action name that changes between Show password and Hide password (or supplied labels), and aria-controls referencing the native input. Its decorative icon is hidden from assistive technology.

Activating the native visibility button with pointer, Enter or Space changes visibility without submitting the surrounding form or deliberately moving focus away from the button. Normal input and form behavior remains with TextInput and the host.

Effective disabled state disables both input and visibility action. readOnly is forwarded only to the input, deliberately allowing visibility changes without edits. Disabling an already revealed field does not automatically conceal it.

Keep visibility as local instance state through ordinary rerenders. No controlled visibility prop, blur concealment or form-reset visibility handler is provided; a newly mounted instance starts concealed.

Supply a meaningful input label and autocomplete intent appropriate to current or new passwords. Own validation, submission, recovery, authentication and storage; concealment is not encryption or access control.

Preserve input-group styling for TextInput and wrapper-owned icon dimensions; the genuine nested IconButton retains trigger-group styling. Do not override child internals or introduce theme-specific dimensions.

Check keyboard naming, reveal without submission, ref focus, disabled Field integration, read-only reveal and unchanged values across theme changes. Verify dimensions and focus treatment across all four theme/mode mappings rather than treating static markup tests as full acceptance.

limitations: No password strength analysis, authentication, secure storage or asynchronous submission is implemented.
Read-only values remain revealable. Disabled state blocks interaction but does not conceal a previously revealed value.
Visibility is local and not controlled externally; no automatic conceal-on-blur, navigation or form-reset behavior is promised.
Static rendering and linked story code are separate from executed browser, visual or accessibility evidence.
